Document = FrozenSet[int]


@dataclass
class ConformalityReport:
    n: int
    d: int                                    # max document size
    local_level: int                          # largest m with all cliques <= m witnessed
    clique_number: int
    conformal: bool
    minimal_obstructions: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = field(default_factory=list)
    true_faces: int = 0
    flag_faces: int = 0

    @property
    def invented_faces(self) -> int:
        return self.flag_faces - self.true_faces


def _edges(corpus: Sequence[Document]) -> Set[Tuple[int, int]]:
    e: Set[Tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        for x, y in combinations(sorted(doc), 2):
            e.add((x, y))
    return e


def _is_clique(vs: Sequence[int], edges: Set[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bool:
    return all((min(a, b), max(a, b)) in edges for a, b in combinations(vs, 2))


def audit_conformality(corpus: Sequence[Document], n: int) -> ConformalityReport:
    """Full conformality audit of a corpus on the theorem set {0, ..., n-1}."""
    edges = _edges(corpus)
    d = max((len(doc) for doc in corpus), default=0)

    local_level = n
    obstructions: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    clique_number = 0
    true_faces = 0
    flag_faces = 0

    for size in range(1, n + 1):
        witnessed_all = True
        size_obstructions: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
        for cand in combinations(range(n), size):
            if not _is_clique(cand, edges):
                continue
            clique_number = max(clique_number, size)
            flag_faces += 1
            witnessed = any(set(cand) <= set(doc) for doc in corpus)
            if witnessed:
                true_faces += 1
            else:
                witnessed_all = False
                size_obstructions.append(cand)
        if not witnessed_all and local_level == n:
            local_level = size - 1
            obstructions = size_obstructions

    return ConformalityReport(
        n=n,
        d=d,
        local_level=local_level,
        clique_number=clique_number,
        conformal=(local_level == n),
        minimal_obstructions=obstructions,
        true_faces=true_faces,
        flag_faces=flag_faces,
    )


def design(n: int, d: int) -> List[Document]:
    """The complete d-uniform design on n theorems."""
    return [frozenset(c) for c in combinations(range(n), d)]

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations

Face = FrozenSet[int]


def co_citation_complex(corpus: Sequence[Face]) -> Set[Face]:
    """All nonempty subsets of documents."""
    faces: Set[Face] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        items = sorted(doc)
        for size in range(1, len(items) + 1):
            for sub in combinations(items, size):
                faces.add(frozenset(sub))
    return faces


def gf2_rank(rows: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    """Rank over GF(2) of a bitmask-row matrix, by elimination on leading bits."""
    pivots: List[int] = []
    rank = 0
    for row in rows:
        cur = row
        for piv in pivots:
            cur = min(cur, cur ^ piv)
        if cur:
            pivots.append(cur)
            pivots.sort(reverse=True)
            rank += 1
    return rank


def betti_numbers_mod2(corpus: Sequence[Face], max_dim: int) -> List[int]:
    """Betti numbers beta_0, ..., beta_{max_dim} of the co-citation complex over GF(2)."""
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    by_size: Dict[int, List[Face]] = {}
    for face in faces:
        by_size.setdefault(len(face), []).append(face)
    for size in by_size:
        by_size[size].sort(key=lambda f: sorted(f))
    index: Dict[int, Dict[Face, int]] = {
        size: {face: i for i, face in enumerate(fs)} for size, fs in by_size.items()
    }

    def boundary_rank(size: int) -> int:
        if size <= 1 or size not in by_size or (size - 1) not in by_size:
            return 0
        rows: List[int] = []
        for face in by_size[size]:
            mask = 0
            for v in face:
                mask |= 1 << index[size - 1][face - {v}]
            rows.append(mask)
        return gf2_rank(rows)

    return [
        len(by_size.get(k + 1, [])) - boundary_rank(k + 1) - boundary_rank(k + 2)
        for k in range(max_dim + 1)
    ]


def euler_characteristic(corpus: Sequence[Face]) -> int:
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    return sum((-1) ** (len(f) - 1) for f in faces)

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>Corpus Topology Laboratory</h1>
  <p class="sub">
    Six theorems, numbered 0–5. A <b>document</b> is a set of theorems cited together;
    click the buttons to add or remove documents. The <b>co-citation complex</b> is the
    downward closure of the documents — every subset of a bibliography is a face.
    Everything on the right is computed exactly: the face counts
    <span class="mono">f<sub>q</sub></span>, the Euler characteristic
    <span class="mono">χ = f<sub>1</sub> − f<sub>2</sub> + f<sub>3</sub> − …</span>,
    the Betti numbers over the two-element field, and the conformality audit that compares
    the true complex with the flag complex of its pairwise shadow.
  </p>

  <div class="grid">
    <div class="panel">
      <h2>Documents</h2>
      <div class="presets" id="presets"></div>
      <div class="lab">Pairs</div>
      <div class="docgrid" id="pairs"></div>
      <div class="lab">Triples</div>
      <div class="docgrid" id="triples"></div>
      <div class="lab">Larger documents</div>
      <div class="docgrid" id="bigs"></div>
      <svg id="draw" viewBox="0 0 420 330"></svg>
      <p class="hint">
        Shaded blue regions are genuine triangular faces (some document cites all three);
        red dashed regions are triangles that exist only in the pairwise shadow — faces the
        projection invents.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="panel">
      <h2>Measurements</h2>
      <table id="stats"></table>
      <div class="lab">Face counts and the two ceilings</div>
      <table id="faces"></table>
      <div class="lab">Theorems in action</div>
      <div id="checks"></div>
      <div class="lab">Conformality audit</div>
      <div id="conf" style="font-size:13px;line-height:1.6"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
const N = 6;
let docs = [];                       // array of bitmasks

/* ---------- combinatorial helpers ---------- */
function bits(mask){const r=[];for(let i=0;i<N;i++) if(mask>>i&1) r.push(i);return r;}
function popcount(m){let c=0;while(m){c+=m&1;m>>=1;}return c;}
function label(mask){return "{"+bits(mask).join(",")+"}";}
function choose(n,k){if(k<0||k>n)return 0;let r=1;for(let i=1;i<=k;i++)r=r*(n-k+i)/i;return Math.round(r);}
function subsetsOf(mask){        // all nonempty submasks
  const out=[];for(let s=mask;s>0;s=(s-1)&mask) out.push(s);return out;
}

/* ---------- the complex ---------- */
function complex(){
  const set=new Set();
  for(const d of docs) for(const s of subsetsOf(d)) set.add(s);
  return [...set];
}
function fVector(faces){
  const f=new Array(N+1).fill(0);
  for(const s of faces) f[popcount(s)]++;
  return f;
}
/* ---------- GF(2) homology ---------- */
function gf2rank(rows){
  const piv=[];let rank=0;
  for(let r of rows){
    let cur=r;
    for(const p of piv){ const x=cur^p; if(x<cur) cur=x; }
    if(cur){piv.push(cur);piv.sort((a,b)=>b-a);rank++;}
  }
  return rank;
}
function betti(faces,maxDim){
  const bySize={};
  for(const s of faces){const k=popcount(s);(bySize[k]=bySize[k]||[]).push(s);}
  const idx={};
  for(const k in bySize){bySize[k].sort((a,b)=>a-b);idx[k]={};bySize[k].forEach((s,i)=>idx[k][s]=i);}
  function brank(size){
    if(size<=1||!bySize[size]||!bySize[size-1]) return 0;
    const rows=bySize[size].map(s=>{
      let m=0n;
      for(const v of bits(s)) m|=1n<<BigInt(idx[size-1][s^(1<<v)]);
      return m;
    });
    // BigInt elimination
    const piv=[];let rank=0;
    for(let r of rows){
      let cur=r;
      for(const p of piv){const x=cur^p; if(x<cur) cur=x;}
      if(cur){piv.push(cur);piv.sort((a,b)=>(b>a?1:b<a?-1:0));rank++;}
    }
    return rank;
  }
  const out=[];
  for(let k=0;k<=maxDim;k++){
    const dim=(bySize[k+1]||[]).length;
    out.push(dim-brank(k+1)-brank(k+2));
  }
  return out;
}
/* ---------- pairwise shadow ---------- */
function edgeSet(){
  const e=new Set();
  for(const d of docs){const b=bits(d);
    for(let i=0;i<b.length;i++)for(let j=i+1;j<b.length;j++) e.add(b[i]*N+b[j]);}
  return e;
}
function isClique(mask,e){
  const b=bits(mask);
  for(let i=0;i<b.length;i++)for(let j=i+1;j<b.length;j++)
    if(!e.has(b[i]*N+b[j])) return false;
  return true;
}
function witnessed(mask){return docs.some(d=>(mask&~d)===0);}
function support(){return docs.reduce((a,m)=>a|m,0);}
function audit(){
  const e=edgeSet(), sup=support(), nsup=popcount(sup);
  let level=nsup, obstructions=[], cliqueNum=0, flag=0;
  for(let size=1;size<=nsup;size++){
    let ok=true, bad=[];
    for(let m=1;m<(1<<N);m++){
      if(popcount(m)!==size || (m & ~sup)) continue;
      if(!isClique(m,e)) continue;
      cliqueNum=Math.max(cliqueNum,size); flag++;
      if(!witnessed(m)){ok=false;bad.push(m);}
    }
    if(!ok && level===nsup){level=size-1;obstructions=bad;}
  }
  return {level,obstructions,cliqueNum,flag,nsup};
}

/* ---------- rendering ---------- */
const P=[];
for(let i=0;i<N;i++){const a=-Math.PI/2+2*Math.PI*i/N;
  P.push([210+140*Math.cos(a),165+130*Math.sin(a)]);}

function draw(){
  const e=edgeSet(), faces=new Set(complex());
  let s='';
  // triangles
  for(let m=1;m<(1<<N);m++){
    if(popcount(m)!==3) continue;
    const b=bits(m), pts=b.map(v=>P[v].join(",")).join(" ");
    if(faces.has(m))
      s+=`<polygon points="${pts}" fill="#6ea8fe" opacity="0.16"/>`;
    else if(isClique(m,e))
      s+=`<polygon points="${pts}" fill="#ff8a7a" opacity="0.10" stroke="#ff8a7a"
           stroke-dasharray="4 4" stroke-width="1"/>`;
  }
  // edges
  for(const key of e){const x=Math.floor(key/N), y=key%N;
    s+=`<line x1="${P[x][0]}" y1="${P[x][1]}" x2="${P[y][0]}" y2="${P[y][1]}"
         stroke="#8fa6d8" stroke-width="1.8" opacity="0.85"/>`;}
  // vertices
  for(let i=0;i<N;i++){
    s+=`<circle cx="${P[i][0]}" cy="${P[i][1]}" r="15" fill="#171b26" stroke="#6ea8fe"
         stroke-width="2"/>`;
    s+=`<text x="${P[i][0]}" y="${P[i][1]+5}" text-anchor="middle" fill="#e8ecf5"
         font-size="14" font-family="ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace">${i}</text>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('draw').innerHTML=s;
}

function row(k,v){return `<tr><td>${k}</td><td class="mono num">${v}</td></tr>`;}

function refresh(){
  document.querySelectorAll('button[data-mask]').forEach(b=>{
    b.classList.toggle('on', docs.includes(+b.dataset.mask));
  });
  const faces=complex(), f=fVector(faces);
  const d=docs.reduce((a,m)=>Math.max(a,popcount(m)),0);
  const chi=f.reduce((a,c,q)=>q===0?a:a+((q%2===1)?c:-c),0);
  const maxDim=Math.max(0,d-1);
  const be=betti(faces,Math.max(maxDim,2));
  const A=audit();

  document.getElementById('stats').innerHTML=
    row("documents  <i>N</i>",docs.length)+
    row("document-size bound  <i>d</i>",d)+
    row("faces (nonempty)",faces.length)+
    row("Euler characteristic  χ",chi)+
    row("Betti numbers (mod 2)","["+be.join(", ")+"]")+
    row("∑(−1)<sup>k</sup>β<sub>k</sub>",
        be.reduce((a,b,k)=>a+(k%2?-b:b),0));

  let ftab='<tr><th>q</th><th class="num">f<sub>q</sub></th>'+
           '<th class="num">budget N·C(d,q)</th>'+
           '<th class="num">ceiling C(6,q)</th></tr>';
  for(let q=1;q<=N;q++){
    if(f[q]===0 && q>Math.max(d,1)) continue;
    ftab+=`<tr><td class="mono">${q}</td><td class="mono num">${f[q]}</td>`+
          `<td class="mono num">${docs.length*choose(d,q)}</td>`+
          `<td class="mono num">${choose(N,q)}</td></tr>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('faces').innerHTML=ftab;

  const checks=[];
  const vanish=be.every((b,k)=>k<d||b===0);
  checks.push([vanish,
    `<b>Support theorem.</b> No homology in dimensions ≥ d = ${d}: every
     β<sub>k</sub> with k ≥ ${d} is zero.`]);
  let budgetOK=true;
  for(let q=1;q<=N;q++) if(f[q]>docs.length*choose(d,q)) budgetOK=false;
  checks.push([budgetOK,
    `<b>Document budget.</b> f<sub>q</sub> ≤ N·C(d,q) for every q — a bound
     that never mentions the number of theorems.`]);
  const ep=be.reduce((a,b,k)=>a+(k%2?-b:b),0)===chi;
  checks.push([ep,`<b>Euler–Poincaré.</b> The alternating sum of Betti numbers
     equals the alternating sum of face counts.`]);
  document.getElementById('checks').innerHTML=checks.map(([ok,txt])=>
    `<div class="check"><span class="badge ${ok?'pass':'fail'}">${ok?'HOLDS':'FAILS'}</span>
     <span>${txt}</span></div>`).join('');

  const invented=A.flag-faces.length;
  let ctext=`Audited over the ${A.nsup} theorems that are actually cited. Clique number of the pairwise shadow: <span class="mono">${A.cliqueNum}</span>.
    Locally conformal up to level <span class="mono">${A.level}</span>
    ${A.level>=A.nsup?'— the corpus is <b>conformal</b>.':''}<br>
    True faces <span class="mono">${faces.length}</span>, flag-complex faces
    <span class="mono">${A.flag}</span>, invented by the projection
    <span class="mono" style="color:${invented?'#ff8a7a':'#6ee7a8'}">${invented}</span>.`;
  if(A.obstructions.length){
    ctext+=`<br>Smallest witness-free cliques: <span class="mono">`+
      A.obstructions.slice(0,8).map(label).join(" ")+
      (A.obstructions.length>8?" …":"")+`</span>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('conf').innerHTML=ctext;
  draw();
}

/* ---------- build controls ---------- */
function addButtons(containerId,size){
  const c=document.getElementById(containerId);
  for(let m=1;m<(1<<N);m++){
    if(size==='big'? popcount(m)<4 : popcount(m)!==size) continue;
    const b=document.createElement('button');
    b.textContent=label(m); b.dataset.mask=m;
    b.onclick=()=>{const v=+b.dataset.mask;
      docs=docs.includes(v)?docs.filter(x=>x!==v):docs.concat(v);refresh();};
    c.appendChild(b);
  }
}
addButtons('pairs',2); addButtons('triples',3); addButtons('bigs','big');

const PRESETS={
  "Hollow triangle (the classical obstruction)":[0b000011,0b000101,0b000110],
  "Filled triangle (one document)":[0b000111],
  "Pairwise design D(6,2)":Array.from({length:64},(_,m)=>m).filter(m=>popcount(m)===2),
  "Triple design D(6,3)":Array.from({length:64},(_,m)=>m).filter(m=>popcount(m)===3),
  "Sparse 6-cycle":[0b000011,0b000110,0b001100,0b011000,0b110000,0b100001],
  "Hollow tetrahedron on 0-3":[0b000111,0b001011,0b001101,0b001110],
  "Clear":[]
};
const pc=document.getElementById('presets');
for(const name in PRESETS){
  const b=document.createElement('button');
  b.textContent=name;
  b.onclick=()=>{docs=PRESETS[name].slice();refresh();};
  pc.appendChild(b);
}
docs=PRESETS["Hollow triangle (the classical obstruction)"].slice();
refresh();
</script>

    },
    {
      "title": "Extremal Betti Explorer: Where the n^d Mass Goes",
      "description": "Two sliders - the theorem count n and the document-size bound d - drive the complete extremal profile of the complete d-uniform design. A log-scale bar chart shows the chain dimensions C(n,k+1) with the realised Betti numbers as gold markers, making the abrupt end of the support at dimension d-1 unmistakable; a log-log growth panel tracks the top Betti number C(n-1,d) against the total of everything beneath it as n varies, with the current n marked. A live table lists the two certified inequalities - the concentration bound |chi| <= d max_k beta_k and the localised bound (n-d)^d <= d!(beta_{d-1} + (d-1)n^{d-1} + 1) - with both sides evaluated and a pass badge, together with the number of documents C(n,d) such a corpus would require, which is the reason no real literature is ever extremal.",

<script>
function choose(n,k){ if(k<0||k>n||n<0) return 0; let r=1;
  for(let i=1;i<=k;i++) r=r*(n-k+i)/i; return Math.round(r); }
function fact(k){let r=1;for(let i=2;i<=k;i++)r*=i;return r;}
function fmt(x){
  if(!isFinite(x)) return "∞";
  if(Math.abs(x)>=1e7) return x.toExponential(2).replace("e+","×10<sup>")+"</sup>";
  return Math.round(x).toLocaleString("en-US");
}

function profile(n,d){
  const f=[]; for(let q=1;q<=d;q++) f.push(choose(n,q));
  const chi=1-Math.pow(-1,d)*choose(n-1,d);
  const beta=new Array(d).fill(0); beta[0]+=1; beta[d-1]+=choose(n-1,d);
  return {f,chi,beta};
}

function barChart(n,d,P){
  const W=460,H=260,L=44,B=34,T=14,R=10;
  const vals=P.f.concat(P.beta.filter(x=>x>0));
  const maxV=Math.max(...P.f,1), minV=1;
  const lg=v=>Math.log10(Math.max(v,0.6));
  const y=v=>H-B-(lg(v)-lg(minV))/(lg(maxV*1.6)-lg(minV))*(H-B-T);
  const kmax=Math.max(d,1), bw=(W-L-R)/kmax*0.62, step=(W-L-R)/kmax;
  let s=`<rect x="0" y="0" width="${W}" height="${H}" fill="none"/>`;
  for(let e=0;e<=Math.ceil(lg(maxV));e++){
    const yy=y(Math.pow(10,e));
    s+=`<line x1="${L}" y1="${yy}" x2="${W-R}" y2="${yy}" stroke="#232a3a"/>`;
    s+=`<text x="${L-6}" y="${yy+4}" text-anchor="end" fill="#98a3bb" font-size="10">
        10<tspan dy="-4" font-size="8">${e}</tspan></text>`;
  }
  for(let k=0;k<d;k++){
    const x=L+step*k+(step-bw)/2, yy=y(P.f[k]);
    s+=`<rect x="${x}" y="${yy}" width="${bw}" height="${H-B-yy}" fill="#6ea8fe"
         opacity="0.42" rx="2"/>`;
    if(P.beta[k]>0)
      s+=`<circle cx="${x+bw/2}" cy="${y(P.beta[k])}" r="5.5" fill="#f0b429"/>`;
    s+=`<text x="${x+bw/2}" y="${H-B+15}" text-anchor="middle" fill="#98a3bb"
         font-size="11">${k}</text>`;
  }
  // the vanishing region

### A guided tour of the extremal topology of co-citation complexes

---

## 1. From bibliographies to shapes

A bibliography is not a list of arrows. When a paper cites results $A$, $B$ and $C$ together it asserts a *simultaneous relevance* among them that no pairwise relation records. So model a body of literature as a **corpus**: a finite family of finite sets of theorems, one set per document.

From a corpus we build a shape. Declare every subset of a bibliography to be a *face*, and you obtain the **co-citation complex** — points, edges, triangles, tetrahedra, glued exactly where authors have thought about things together.

> **Definition.** The co-citation complex of a corpus $\mathcal C$ on a theorem set $V$ is
> $$X(\mathcal C) = \{\, S \subseteq V : S \subseteq W \text{ for some } W \in \mathcal C \,\}.$$
> We write $f_q$ for the number of faces with exactly $q$ vertices; a face with $q$ vertices has dimension $q-1$.

The holes of this shape are what everyone wants to measure. A one-dimensional hole is a loop of co-citation that never closes: $A$ and $B$ appear together, $B$ and $C$, $C$ and $A$, but no single document brings all three into the same frame. Counting holes in each dimension gives the **Betti numbers** $\beta_0, \beta_1, \beta_2, \dots$

<details>
<summary><b>Refresher: what a Betti number actually counts</b></summary>

Fix a field of coefficients. The $k$-th chain group is the vector space spanned by the faces with $k+1$ vertices, so its dimension is $f_{k+1}$. The boundary map $\partial_k$ sends a face to the (signed) sum of its facets, and satisfies $\partial_{k}\circ\partial_{k+1} = 0$. Then
$$\beta_k = \dim \ker \partial_k - \operatorname{rank}\partial_{k+1} = f_{k+1} - \operatorname{rank}\partial_k - \operatorname{rank}\partial_{k+1}.$$
Two facts follow immediately and are the *only* two we will use:

* **(P1)** $\beta_k \le f_{k+1}$ — you cannot have more holes than cells;
* **(P2)** $\sum_k (-1)^k\beta_k = \sum_k (-1)^k f_{k+1}$ — the Euler–Poincaré relation.

Everything below is proved from (P1) and (P2) alone, so it holds for *every* coefficient field simultaneously. See [simplicial homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplicial_homology) for the full construction.
</details>

**Play first, theory second.** Below is a laboratory on six theorems. Click documents on and off; the complex, its Euler characteristic, its Betti numbers over the two-element field, and a full conformality audit are recomputed exactly, on the spot. Start with the preset *Hollow triangle*: three documents, each citing one pair, producing a genuine one-dimensional hole. Then press *Filled triangle*, where a single document cites all three, and watch $\beta_1$ drop to zero.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Three things to try in the laboratory before reading on:

1. **The support experiment.** Load *Pairwise design D(6,2)* — every pair of theorems is a document. Note that $f_3 = 0$: there are no triangles at all, and $\beta_2 = 0$ necessarily. Now load *Triple design D(6,3)* and triangles appear. Bibliography length, and nothing else, decides which dimensions can exist.
2. **The invented faces.** In *Hollow triangle*, the pairwise shadow has a triangle the corpus does not. The red dashed region is a face the projection invents.
3. **The budget.** In *Sparse 6-cycle* — six documents, each a pair — compare $f_2 = 6$ with the ambient ceiling $\binom62 = 15$. Few documents, few faces, regardless of how many theorems exist.

---

## 2. The parameter nobody was tracking

Write $n$ for the number of theorems and $d$ for the largest bibliography. Every claim in the folklore literature is phrased in terms of $n$. The first theorem says $n$ is almost irrelevant.

> **Support Theorem.** If every document cites at most $d$ theorems, then $f_q = 0$ for all $q > d$, and hence
> $$\beta_k = 0 \quad\text{for all } k \ge d,$$
> for every coefficient field.

<details>
<summary><b>Proof (one line)</b></summary>

A face is a subset of some document's bibliography, so it has at most $d$ elements. There is therefore no chain group in degree $\ge d$, and a hole needs cells to be made of. $\square$
</details>

A corpus of a billion theorems whose papers cite at most twenty results has, unconditionally, no topology above dimension nineteen. Not "typically none" — none.

---

## 3. How much topology can there possibly be?

If $d$ is the ceiling, what is the richest corpus that respects it? The answer is the most symmetric object imaginable: the **complete design** $\mathcal D_{n,d}$, in which *every* $d$-element set of theorems is somebody's bibliography. Its complex is the $(d-1)$-skeleton of a simplex, so $f_q = \binom nq$ for all $q \le d$.

> **Extremal Counting Theorem.** Among all corpora on $n$ theorems with documents of size at most $d$, the maximum possible $f_q$ is exactly $\binom nq$ for $q \le d$, attained by the complete design.

Counting cells is not counting holes, though: a solid ball has plenty of cells and no holes. The bridge is the **Euler characteristic** $\chi = f_1 - f_2 + f_3 - \cdots$, which by (P2) can equally be read off the holes.

> **Euler Characteristic of the Design.** For $1\le d\le n$,
> $$\chi(\mathcal D_{n,d}) = 1 - (-1)^d\binom{n-1}{d}.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Proof sketch, and the binomial identity behind it</b></summary>

Truncate the alternating sum at $d$ (there is nothing above), reindex, and apply the *partial* alternating binomial identity
$$\sum_{j=0}^{d}(-1)^j\binom{m+1}{j} = (-1)^d\binom{m}{d},$$
which follows by induction from Pascal's rule $\binom{m+1}{d+1} = \binom md + \binom m{d+1}$. Sanity checks: the hollow triangle $(n,d)=(3,2)$ gives $\chi = 0 = 3-3$; the $2$-skeleton of the $4$-simplex $(n,d)=(5,3)$ gives $\chi = 5 = 5-10+10$.
</details>

Now the pigeonhole that carries the whole theory. The design's Euler characteristic has magnitude $\Theta(n^d)$ — but by the Support Theorem only $d$ Betti numbers are allowed to be nonzero at all. An alternating sum of $d$ numbers cannot be huge unless one of them is.

> **Concentration.** In any $d$-bounded corpus, some $k < d$ has $|\chi| \le d\,\beta_k$. For the design this gives $(n-d)^d \le d!\,d\,\beta_k + d!$.
>
> **Localisation.** Moreover $|\chi| \le \beta_{d-1} + \sum_{k<d-1} f_{k+1}$, and for the design
> $$(n-d)^d \le d!\left(\beta_{d-1} + (d-1)n^{d-1} + 1\right).$$

The correction term is $O(n^{d-1})$ while the left-hand side is $\Theta(n^d)$: the mass cannot hide in the low dimensions, because each of them is capped by its own chain dimension. **The extremal homology sits in the single dimension $d-1$, at order $n^d$, and is exactly zero above.**

The explorer below makes this concrete. Slide $n$ and $d$ and watch the gold dot — the top Betti number — separate from everything beneath it.

<details>
<summary><b>Why this is the only correct form of the "power law"</b></summary>

The folklore claim is that $\beta_k$ grows polynomially in the corpus size, with a freely fitted exponent. What is true is: (i) $\beta_k = 0$ for $k \ge d$ always; (ii) $\beta_k \le \binom{n}{k+1}$ always; (iii) the exponent $d$ is attained only in dimension $d-1$ and only by a corpus with $\binom nd$ documents. The exponent is not a free parameter fitted to data — it is pinned to the top surviving dimension by the bibliography bound.
</details>

## 4. Real corpora are nowhere near the ceiling

The design needs $\binom nd$ documents — astronomically more papers than theorems. What does actual sparsity buy? A change of accounting: count faces *by document* rather than by subsets of theorems.

> **Document Budget.** A $d$-bounded corpus with $N$ documents satisfies
> $$f_q \le N\binom dq, \qquad \beta_k \le N\binom{d}{k+1}.$$
> Neither bound mentions the number of theorems.

<details>
<summary><b>Proof, and why it is the practically useful bound</b></summary>

Every $q$-face is a $q$-subset of some document, so the $q$-faces lie inside $\bigcup_{W}\binom Wq$, whose size is at most $\sum_W \binom{|W|}{q} \le N\binom dq$. Then apply (P1).

Consequence: if the document count grows more slowly than $n^{k+1}$, the normalised Betti number $\beta_k/\binom{n}{k+1}$ tends to zero. Turned around, staying at the ceiling demands $N \ge \binom nq/\binom dq$ documents. There is no cheap route to a topologically rich literature.
</details>

The starkest explicit case: a purely pairwise corpus on $n \ge 4$ theorems with at most $n$ documents has $\beta_1 < \binom n2$ — missing the ceiling by an order of magnitude ($n$ against $n^2$), even though dimension $1$ is the only dimension it can support.

## 5. The pairwise shadow lies — at every level

Most pipelines never see bibliographies. They see the **co-citation graph** (an edge whenever two theorems are cited together) and rebuild the complex as its **flag complex** (fill in every clique). When is that faithful? The corpus is called *conformal* when the two complexes agree.

The classical warning example is the hollow triangle you met in §1. The folklore treats it as *the* obstruction. It is only the first rung.

> **Hierarchy Theorem.** For every level $m \ge 2$ there is a corpus in which every clique of at most $m$ theorems has a common witnessing document, while some clique of $m+1$ theorems has none. No fixed amount of local checking certifies conformality.

<details>
<summary><b>The witnesses, and why the pairwise shadow of a design is blind</b></summary>

Take the design $\mathcal D_{m+1,m}$. Any two theorems lie in a common $m$-set, so the co-citation graph is *complete*: the projection has destroyed all information. Every group of $m$ theorems has a document; the full set of $m+1$ has none. The hollow triangle is exactly the case $m = 2$, that is $\mathcal D_{3,2}$.

Quantitatively, for $2 \le d < n$ the flag complex of $\mathcal D_{n,d}$ has all $2^n$ subsets as faces against a true count of $\sum_{q\le d}\binom nq$, so the projection invents $2^n - \sum_{q\le d}\binom nq$ of them.
</details>

> **Structure Theorem.** For a $d$-bounded corpus, conformality is equivalent to the conjunction of (i) every clique has at most $d$ vertices, and (ii) every clique of size at most $d$ has a witnessing document. Condition (ii) is checkable locally; condition (i) is irreducibly global.

---

## 6. What the holes are not

Finally the application everyone wants: reading research communities off the topology. Call a labelling rule **uniform** if renaming the theorems renames its output correspondingly — that is, if it uses the incidence pattern and nothing else. Every rule built from homology, persistence, spectra or clique structure is uniform.

> **Non-Identifiability Theorem.** On a corpus whose incidence pattern is symmetric enough that some renaming carries any chosen theorem to any other, every uniform rule outputs a constant labelling. It therefore disagrees with every ground truth that distinguishes even two theorems.

<details>
<summary><b>Proof (three lines), and the choice of witness</b></summary>

Given $x, y$, pick a renaming $\sigma$ with $\sigma\mathcal C = \mathcal C$ and $\sigma x = y$. Uniformity gives $R(\mathcal C)(y) = R(\sigma\mathcal C)(\sigma x) = R(\mathcal C)(x)$. $\square$

The force lies in the witness. One might hope the obstruction bites only on degenerate corpora. The complete designs are the opposite: invariant under *every* permutation of theorems, and by §3 the most topologically rich corpora available. The pairwise design has $\beta_1 = \binom{n-1}{2}$, positive from three theorems onwards. A corpus dripping with holes, and not one of them knows what its theorems mean.

Read in reverse: a rule that *does* recover a non-constant labelling — say, one that looks up the metadata — is provably not uniform. That is a proof that vertex metadata carries information which cannot be repackaged as incidence data.
</details>

---

## 8. Where this goes next

The honest programme is now sharp enough to be attacked probabilistically:

* **A null model.** For a sparse random corpus with bounded expected document size, does each fixed-dimensional normalised Betti number converge to a deterministic limit? The document budget forces $0$ in the subpolynomial regime; the interesting regime is the matched one, where boundary ranks — not face counts — decide.
* **Conformality thresholds.** In a growing random corpus, at what density does every clique acquire a common witness? The Structure Theorem names the two events to track, and the Hierarchy Theorem shows the threshold must be indexed by a witness level.
* **Persistent change detection.** The co-citation complex of a growing corpus is monotone, hence a filtration. Does a rise and decay in persistent second homology detect sustained failure of local conformality more reliably than raw triangle counts?
* **Uniqueness of the extremal corpus.** Attaining the ceiling needs $\Omega\left(\binom nq/\binom dq\right)$ documents. Is the design the only corpus that does it, up to redundancy?
* **Identifiability under assortativity.** Exact uniform recovery is impossible. Under a generative model with latent communities, at what signal strength does approximate recovery begin, and does homology contribute anything beyond [graph connectivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_structure)?

The shape of a library is real. It is just smaller, more constrained, and less talkative than we had hoped — and now we know exactly by how much.

/-! ## Local conformality -/

/-- `LocallyConformal C m`: every clique of at most `m` theorems in the pairwise
co-citation graph is covered by a single document. -/
def LocallyConformal (C : Corpus V) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset V, S.card ≤ m → (coCitationGraph C).IsClique (↑S : Set V) → ∃ W ∈ C, S ⊆ W

omit [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] in
theorem locallyConformal_of_conformal {C : Corpus V} (h : Conformal C) (m : ℕ) :
    LocallyConformal C m := fun S _ hS => h S hS

omit [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] in
theorem locallyConformal_mono {C : Corpus V} {m m' : ℕ} (hmm : m ≤ m')
    (h : LocallyConformal C m') : LocallyConformal C m :=
  fun S hS hclique => h S (hS.trans hmm) hclique

omit [DecidableEq V] in
/-- Conformality is exactly local conformality at the level of the whole theorem set. -/
theorem conformal_iff_locallyConformal_card (C : Corpus V) :

  exact h S (by simpa using Finset.card_le_univ S) hS

/-! ## The design corpus is maximally non-conformal -/

/-- With documents of size at least two, the pairwise co-citation graph of the design is
complete: the two-section retains no information about the design. -/
theorem coCitationGraph_skeletonCorpus {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hdn : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    coCitationGraph (skeletonCorpus V d) = ⊤ := by
  ext x y
  simp only [coCitationGraph, SimpleGraph.top_adj]
  refine ⟨fun h => h.1, fun hxy => ⟨hxy, ?_⟩⟩
  have hcard : ({x, y} : Finset V).card ≤ d := by
    rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (by simpa using hxy), Finset.card_singleton]
    omega
  obtain ⟨W, hsub, hWcard⟩ := Finset.exists_superset_card_eq hcard hdn
  exact ⟨W, Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, hWcard⟩,
    hsub (by simp), hsub (by simp)⟩

/-- The design corpus is locally conformal at its own document size: every set of at most
`d` theorems — clique or not — is covered by a document. -/
theorem locallyConformal_skeletonCorpus {d : ℕ} (hdn : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    LocallyConformal (skeletonCorpus V d) d := by
  intro S hS _
  obtain ⟨W, hsub, hWcard⟩ := Finset.exists_superset_card_eq hS hdn
  exact ⟨W, Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, hWcard⟩, hsub⟩

/-- ... and it fails to be locally conformal one level higher. -/
theorem not_locallyConformal_skeletonCorpus_succ {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (hdn : d + 1 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ¬ LocallyConformal (skeletonCorpus V d) (d + 1) := by
  intro hloc
  obtain ⟨S, -, hScard⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_superset_card_eq (s := (∅ : Finset V)) (by simp) hdn
  have hclique : (coCitationGraph (skeletonCorpus V d)).IsClique (↑S : Set V) := by
    rw [coCitationGraph_skeletonCorpus hd (by omega)]
    intro a _ b _ hab
    simpa using hab
  obtain ⟨W, hW, hSW⟩ := hloc S (le_of_eq hScard) hclique
  have := Finset.card_le_card hSW
  rw [hScard, (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hW).2] at this
  omega

/-- **Hierarchy theorem.** For every level `m ≥ 2` there is a theorem corpus in which every
clique of at most `m` theorems has a common witnessing document, while some clique of
`m + 1` theorems has none.  Consequently no fixed level of local witness checking implies
conformality, and the catalogued three-theorem boundary corpus is only the case `m = 2` of
an infinite strictly increasing family of obstructions. -/
theorem strict_hierarchy_of_local_conformality (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    ∃ C : Corpus (Fin (m + 1)),
      LocallyConformal C m ∧ ¬ LocallyConformal C (m + 1) ∧ ¬ Conformal C := by
  have hcard : Fintype.card (Fin (m + 1)) = m + 1 := Fintype.card_fin _
  refine ⟨skeletonCorpus (Fin (m + 1)) m, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact locallyConformal_skeletonCorpus (by omega)
  · exact not_locallyConformal_skeletonCorpus_succ hm (by omega)
  · intro hconf
    exact not_locallyConformal_skeletonCorpus_succ hm (by omega)
      (locallyConformal_of_conformal hconf (m + 1))

/-! ## The sharp document-size threshold for the design -/

/-- **Sharp threshold.** For `2 ≤ d ≤ n` the complete `d`-uniform design is conformal if and
only if its documents already cover the whole theorem set, i.e. `d = n`.  Conformality of
the extremal corpus is an all-or-nothing event located exactly at document size `n`. -/
theorem conformal_skeletonCorpus_iff {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hdn : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    Conformal (skeletonCorpus V d) ↔ Fintype.card V ≤ d := by
  constructor
  · intro hconf
    by_contra hlt
    push_neg at hlt
    exact not_locallyConformal_skeletonCorpus_succ hd (by omega)
      (locallyConformal_of_conformal hconf (d + 1))
  · intro hn S _
    have hdeq : d = Fintype.card V := le_antisymm hdn hn
    refine ⟨Finset.univ, ?_, Finset.subset_univ _⟩
    exact Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, by
      simpa [Finset.card_univ] using hdeq.symm⟩

/-- **Structure of conformality for bounded corpora.**  If every document cites at most `d`
theorems, conformality is equivalent to the conjunction of a clique-number condition and
local conformality at level `d`.  The clique-number condition is the genuinely global part:
local checking alone can never supply it, by the hierarchy theorem. -/
theorem conformal_iff_of_bounded {C : Corpus V} {d : ℕ} (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) :
    Conformal C ↔

open Classical Finset
open TheoremNetworkTopology

namespace CorpusBettiExtremal

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-! ## Document-size bounded corpora -/

/-- `BoundedCorpus C d` says every document of the corpus cites at most `d` theorems. -/
def BoundedCorpus (C : Corpus V) (d : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ W ∈ C, W.card ≤ d

/-- A `d`-bounded corpus has no face with more than `d` vertices. -/
theorem facesOfCard_eq_empty_of_bounded {C : Corpus V} {d q : ℕ}
    (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) (hq : d < q) : facesOfCard C q = ∅ := by
  refine Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mpr fun S hS => ?_
  rw [facesOfCard, Finset.mem_filter, coCitationComplex, Finset.mem_filter] at hS
  obtain ⟨⟨-, W, hW, hSW⟩, hcard⟩ := hS
  exact absurd ((hcard ▸ Finset.card_le_card hSW).trans (hC W hW)) (by omega)

/-- **Sharpened dimension obstruction.** Every rank-presented Betti number of a `d`-bounded
corpus vanishes in homological dimensions `k ≥ d`, no matter how many theorems there are. -/
theorem bettiFromRanks_eq_zero_of_bounded {C : Corpus V} {d k : ℕ}
    (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) (boundaryRank : ℕ → ℕ) (hk : d ≤ k) :
    bettiFromRanks C boundaryRank k = 0 := by
  unfold bettiFromRanks
  rw [facesOfCard_eq_empty_of_bounded hC (by omega)]
  simp

/-! ## The complete `d`-uniform design -/

/-- The *design corpus*: every `d`-element set of theorems is a document.  This is the
maximally symmetric `d`-bounded corpus. -/
def skeletonCorpus (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (d : ℕ) : Corpus V :=
  Finset.univ.powersetCard d

theorem boundedCorpus_skeletonCorpus (d : ℕ) :
    BoundedCorpus (skeletonCorpus V d) d := by
  intro W hW
  exact le_of_eq (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hW).2

/-- The complex generated by the design is the full `(d-1)`-skeleton of the simplex on the
theorem set. -/
theorem mem_coCitationComplex_skeletonCorpus {d : ℕ} (hd : d ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (S : Finset V) :
    S ∈ coCitationComplex (skeletonCorpus V d) ↔ S.card ≤ d := by
  rw [coCitationComplex, Finset.mem_filter]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨-, W, hW, hSW⟩
    exact (Finset.card_le_card hSW).trans (le_of_eq (Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hW).2)
  · intro hcard
    refine ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.mpr (Finset.subset_univ _), ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨W, hSW, hWcard⟩ := Finset.exists_superset_card_eq hcard hd
    exact ⟨W, Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, hWcard⟩, hSW⟩

/-- For `q ≤ d ≤ n` the `q`-faces of the design are *all* `q`-element sets of theorems. -/
theorem facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus {d q : ℕ} (hqd : q ≤ d) (hd : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    facesOfCard (skeletonCorpus V d) q = Finset.univ.powersetCard q := by
  ext S
  rw [facesOfCard, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powersetCard,
    mem_coCitationComplex_skeletonCorpus hd]
  exact ⟨fun h => ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, h.2⟩, fun h => ⟨h.2 ▸ hqd, h.2⟩⟩

theorem card_facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus {d q : ℕ} (hqd : q ≤ d) (hd : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    (facesOfCard (skeletonCorpus V d) q).card = (Fintype.card V).choose q := by
  rw [facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus hqd hd, Finset.card_powersetCard, Finset.card_univ]

/-- **Sharp extremal face count.** Among all corpora whose documents cite at most `d`
theorems, the largest possible number of `q`-element faces is exactly `C(n, q)` whenever
`q ≤ d ≤ n`, and the complete `d`-uniform design attains it. -/
theorem isGreatest_card_facesOfCard_bounded {d q : ℕ} (hqd : q ≤ d)
    (hd : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    IsGreatest {m : ℕ | ∃ C : Corpus V, BoundedCorpus C d ∧ (facesOfCard C q).card = m}
      ((Fintype.card V).choose q) := by
  constructor
  · exact ⟨skeletonCorpus V d, boundedCorpus_skeletonCorpus d,
      card_facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus hqd hd⟩
  · rintro m ⟨C, -, rfl⟩
    exact card_facesOfCard_le_choose C q

/-- Polynomial lower bound for the extremal face count: after scaling by `q !` it is at
least `(n - q)^q`.  With the binomial ceiling this shows the extremal `f`-vector entry has
order exactly `n^q`. -/
theorem pow_le_card_facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus {d q : ℕ} (hqd : q ≤ d)
    (hd : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    (Fintype.card V - q) ^ q
      ≤ q.factorial * (facesOfCard (skeletonCorpus V d) q).card := by
  rw [card_facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus hqd hd, ← Nat.descFactorial_eq_factorial_mul_choose]
  exact (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) q).trans
    (Nat.pow_sub_le_descFactorial (Fintype.card V) q)

/-! ## Euler characteristic of the design complex -/

/-- Partial alternating binomial sum: `∑_{j ≤ d} (-1)^j C(m+1, j) = (-1)^d C(m, d)`. -/
theorem alternating_choose_partial (m : ℕ) : ∀ d : ℕ,
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (d + 1), ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ j * ((m + 1).choose j : ℤ)
      = ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ d * (m.choose d : ℤ) := by
  intro d
  induction d with
  | zero => simp
  | succ d ih =>
    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, ih, Nat.choose_succ_succ]
    push_cast
    ring

/-- The Euler characteristic of the co-citation complex, as the alternating sum of the
numbers of faces of each dimension (a face with `q + 1` vertices has dimension `q`). -/
def eulerChar (C : Corpus V) : ℤ :=
  ∑ q ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card V + 1),
    ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ q * ((facesOfCard C (q + 1)).card : ℤ)

/-- **Euler characteristic of the design complex.**  For `1 ≤ d ≤ n` the complete
`d`-uniform design on `n = m + 1` theorems has Euler characteristic `1 - (-1)^d C(m, d)`.
Its absolute value therefore grows like `n^d`. -/
theorem eulerChar_skeletonCorpus {m d : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card V = m + 1)
    (hdn : d ≤ m + 1) :
    eulerChar (skeletonCorpus V d) = 1 - ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ d * (m.choose d : ℤ) := by
  have hd' : d ≤ Fintype.card V := hcard ▸ hdn
  -- kill the terms of dimension `≥ d`
  have htrunc : eulerChar (skeletonCorpus V d)
      = ∑ q ∈ Finset.range d, ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ q *
          ((facesOfCard (skeletonCorpus V d) (q + 1)).card : ℤ) := by
    refine (Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_).symm
    · intro q hq
      simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hq ⊢
      omega
    · intro q _ hq
      simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hq
      rw [facesOfCard_eq_empty_of_bounded (boundedCorpus_skeletonCorpus (V := V) d)
        (by omega)]
      simp
  rw [htrunc]
  have hterm : ∀ q ∈ Finset.range d, ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ q *
      ((facesOfCard (skeletonCorpus V d) (q + 1)).card : ℤ)
        = -(((-1 : ℤ)) ^ (q + 1) * (((m + 1).choose (q + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) := by
    intro q hq
    simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hq
    rw [card_facesOfCard_skeletonCorpus (by omega) hd', hcard]
    ring
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  have hkey := alternating_choose_partial m d
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ'] at hkey
  simp only [pow_zero, Nat.choose_zero_right, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at hkey
  linarith

/-! ## Abstract homology profiles and the extremal lower bound -/

/-- An **abstract Betti profile** of a corpus: a sequence of natural numbers dominated by
the chain dimensions of the co-citation complex and satisfying the Euler–Poincaré relation.

For any coefficient field, the simplicial homology of `coCitationComplex C` provides such a
profile: `dim H_k ≤ dim C_k` is the rank–nullity bound, and the alternating sum of Betti
numbers equals the alternating sum of chain dimensions.  All results below use only these
two properties, so they apply to every coefficient field simultaneously. -/
structure HomologyProfile (C : Corpus V) where
  /-- The Betti numbers. -/
  beta : ℕ → ℕ
  /-- Betti numbers are bounded by the chain dimensions. -/
  le_chain : ∀ k, beta k ≤ (facesOfCard C (k + 1)).card
  /-- The Euler–Poincaré relation. -/
  euler : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card V), ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ k * (beta k : ℤ) = eulerChar C

/-- Every Betti number of a `d`-bounded corpus vanishes in dimensions `≥ d`. -/
theorem HomologyProfile.beta_eq_zero_of_bounded {C : Corpus V} (P : HomologyProfile C)
    {d k : ℕ} (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) (hk : d ≤ k) : P.beta k = 0 := by
  have h := P.le_chain k
  rwa [facesOfCard_eq_empty_of_bounded hC (by omega), Finset.card_empty,
    Nat.le_zero] at h

/-- Every Betti number obeys the binomial ceiling. -/
theorem HomologyProfile.beta_le_choose {C : Corpus V} (P : HomologyProfile C) (k : ℕ) :
    P.beta k ≤ (Fintype.card V).choose (k + 1) :=
  (P.le_chain k).trans (card_facesOfCard_le_choose C (k + 1))

/-- **The Euler characteristic is carried by the surviving dimensions.**  In a `d`-bounded
corpus only the Betti numbers in dimensions `< d` can be nonzero, so the Euler
characteristic is at most their total. -/
theorem HomologyProfile.natAbs_eulerChar_le {C : Corpus V} (P : HomologyProfile C)
    {d : ℕ} (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) (hdn : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    (eulerChar C).natAbs ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range d, P.beta k := by
  -- restrict the Euler–Poincaré sum to the range `[0, d)`
  have hrestrict : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range d, ((-1 : ℤ)) ^ k * (P.beta k : ℤ) = eulerChar C := by
    rw [← P.euler]
    refine Finset.sum_subset ?_ ?_
    · intro k hk
      simp only [Finset.mem_range] at hk ⊢
      omega
    · intro k _ hk
      simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hk
      rw [P.beta_eq_zero_of_bounded hC hk]
      simp
  have habs : |eulerChar C| ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range d, (P.beta j : ℤ) := by
    rw [← hrestrict]
    refine (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _).trans (le_of_eq (Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_))
    intro j _
    rw [abs_mul, abs_pow, abs_neg, abs_one, one_pow, one_mul, Nat.abs_cast]
  rw [Int.abs_eq_natAbs] at habs
  exact_mod_cast habs

/-- **Euler characteristic forces a large Betti number.** In a `d`-bounded corpus only `d`
Betti numbers can be nonzero, so the Euler characteristic — an alternating sum of exactly
those `d` numbers — is at most `d` times the largest of them. -/
theorem HomologyProfile.exists_large_betti {C : Corpus V} (P : HomologyProfile C)
    {d : ℕ} (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) (hd : 0 < d) (hdn : d ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ∃ k < d, (eulerChar C).natAbs ≤ d * P.beta k := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hmax⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_max_image (Finset.range d) P.beta ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hd⟩
  refine ⟨k, Finset.mem_range.mp hk, (P.natAbs_eulerChar_le hC hdn).trans ?_⟩
  calc ∑ j ∈ Finset.range d, P.beta j ≤ ∑ _j ∈ Finset.range d, P.beta k :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun j hj => hmax j hj
    _ = d * P.beta k := by rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_range, smul_eq_mul]

# Sparse corpora: the binomial ceiling is never approached

The research thread conjectures that, in a sparse corpus with bounded expected document
size, each unnormalised Betti number is bounded above by the corresponding binomial face
count and is *typically of strictly smaller order*.  The upper bound is already in the
catalogue.  This file proves the second, sharper half in deterministic form, which is what a
null model would then have to specialise.

The mechanism is a **document budget**: in a `d`-bounded corpus each document can donate at
most `C(d, q)` faces with `q` vertices, so

```
#facesOfCard C q ≤ (number of documents) · C(d, q)
```

and hence every Betti number is bounded by `|C| · C(d, k+1)` — a quantity that does not
involve the number of theorems at all.  Sparsity, in the sense of a document count growing
slower than `n^{k+1}`, therefore forces the normalised Betti number
`β_k / C(n, k+1)` to zero, and the strict inequality `β_k < C(n, k+1)` holds outright.

The smallest concrete instance is proved unconditionally: for a corpus of pairwise
co-citations with at most `n` documents on `n ≥ 4` theorems, `β₁ < C(n, 2)`
(`sparse_betti_one_lt_ceiling`), so the ceiling is strictly missed even though `β₁` is the
one Betti number the pairwise model can support.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (Hypothesizer): (1) the number of documents, not the number of theorems, is the
true budget for chain generators in a bounded corpus; (2) consequently the binomial ceiling
is attained only by corpora with `\Theta(C(n,d))` documents, i.e. by the design corpus of the
extremal file; (3) any corpus with subpolynomially many documents has all normalised Betti
numbers equal to zero in the limit.

Experiment (Experimenter): faces were counted by document rather than by vertex set.  Each
document `W` contributes exactly `C(|W|, q)` sets of `q` vertices, and every face arises this
way, so the total is at most `|C| · C(d, q)`.  For `d = 2` the budget is `|C|` itself: a
pairwise corpus on `n` theorems with `n` documents can support at most `n` independent
one-cycles, against a ceiling of `C(n, 2)`.

Analysis (Analyst): hypotheses (1) and (3) survive as theorems; (2) survives in the weak
direction proved here (attaining the ceiling requires `|C| ≥ C(n,q)/C(d,q)` documents), while
the uniqueness half remains open and is recorded as a future direction.  The bound is tight
in the trivial direction: a corpus consisting of one document of size `d` has exactly
`C(d, q)` faces of size `q`.

Critique (Critic): "sparse" is a hypothesis on the number of documents, not a probabilistic
statement; the theorems below are the deterministic skeleton a random model must inherit,
not a limit law.  The strict inequality is stated for a concrete parameter range rather than
asymptotically, since an asymptotic statement would require a limit formalism that adds no
mathematical content here.

Synthesis (Principal Investigator): the binomial ceiling is a ceiling on the *ambient*
complex; the operative bound for real corpora is the document budget, which is independent
of the theorem count.  This is the missing structural ingredient for a falsifiable null
model.
-- !-- end Lab Notes -- !--
-/

/-- **Document budget.**  In a `d`-bounded corpus the number of faces with `q` vertices is at
most the number of documents times `C(d, q)`: a bound that does not mention the number of
theorems. -/
theorem card_facesOfCard_le_corpus_mul {C : Corpus V} {d : ℕ} (hC : BoundedCorpus C d)
    (q : ℕ) : (facesOfCard C q).card ≤ C.card * d.choose q := by
  have hsub : facesOfCard C q ⊆ C.biUnion fun W => W.powersetCard q := by
    intro S hS
    rw [facesOfCard, Finset.mem_filter, coCitationComplex, Finset.mem_filter] at hS
    obtain ⟨⟨-, W, hW, hSW⟩, hcard⟩ := hS
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨W, hW, Finset.mem_powersetCard.mpr ⟨hSW, hcard⟩⟩
  refine (Finset.card_le_card hsub).trans (Finset.card_biUnion_le.trans ?_)
  calc ∑ W ∈ C, (W.powersetCard q).card = ∑ W ∈ C, W.card.choose q :=
        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun W _ => Finset.card_powersetCard q W
    _ ≤ ∑ _W ∈ C, d.choose q := Finset.sum_le_sum fun W hW => Nat.choose_le_choose q (hC W hW)
    _ = C.card * d.choose q := by rw [Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul]

theorem HomologyProfile_beta_le_corpus_mul {C : Corpus V} (P : HomologyProfile C) {d : ℕ}
    (hC : BoundedCorpus C d) (k : ℕ) : P.beta k ≤ C.card * d.choose (k + 1) :=
  (P.le_chain k).trans (card_facesOfCard_le_corpus_mul hC (k + 1))

face count, every Betti number is strictly below the ceiling. -/

    (hC : BoundedCorpus C d)
    (hsparse : C.card * d.choose (k + 1) < (Fintype.card V).choose (k + 1)) :
    P.beta k < (Fintype.card V).choose (k + 1) :=
  lt_of_le_of_lt (HomologyProfile_beta_le_corpus_mul P hC k) hsparse

/-- `n < C(n, 2)` for `n ≥ 4`: the number of theorems is strictly below the number of

open Classical Finset

namespace CorpusLabelIdentifiability

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-! ## Renaming theorems -/

/-- Renaming the theorems of a corpus by a permutation `σ`. -/
def relabel (σ : Equiv.Perm V) (C : Corpus V) : Corpus V :=
  C.image fun W => W.image σ

/-- A recovery rule is *uniform* when renaming the theorems renames its output
correspondingly: the rule reads the incidence pattern only. -/
def Uniform {L : Type*} (R : Corpus V → V → L) : Prop :=
  ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm V) (C : Corpus V) (v : V), R (relabel σ C) (σ v) = R C v

/-- A corpus is *vertex-transitive* when any theorem can be carried to any other by a
renaming that leaves the corpus unchanged. -/
def VertexTransitive (C : Corpus V) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : V, ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm V, relabel σ C = C ∧ σ x = y

/-! ## The obstruction -/

omit [Fintype V] in
/-- On a vertex-transitive corpus every uniform rule is constant. -/
theorem constant_of_uniform_of_vertexTransitive {L : Type*} (R : Corpus V → V → L)
    (hR : Uniform R) {C : Corpus V} (hC : VertexTransitive C) (x y : V) :
    R C x = R C y := by
  obtain ⟨σ, hσC, hσx⟩ := hC x y
  have h := hR σ C x
  rw [hσC, hσx] at h
  exact h.symm

omit [Fintype V] in
/-- **Non-identifiability.**  No uniform rule can output a non-constant labelling on a
vertex-transitive corpus, so no uniform rule recovers a ground-truth labelling that
distinguishes any two theorems. -/
theorem no_uniform_recovery {L : Type*} (R : Corpus V → V → L) (hR : Uniform R)
    {C : Corpus V} (hC : VertexTransitive C) (lab : V → L) {x y : V}
    (hxy : lab x ≠ lab y) : R C ≠ lab := by
  intro h
  refine hxy ?_
  rw [← h]
  exact constant_of_uniform_of_vertexTransitive R hR hC x y

/-! ## The design corpus is a maximally symmetric witness -/

/-- The family of all `d`-element documents is invariant under every renaming. -/
theorem relabel_skeletonCorpus (σ : Equiv.Perm V) (d : ℕ) :
    relabel σ (skeletonCorpus V d) = skeletonCorpus V d := by
  ext T
  simp only [relabel, skeletonCorpus, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_powersetCard]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨W, ⟨-, hWcard⟩, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨Finset.subset_univ _,
      by rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ σ.injective, hWcard]⟩
  · rintro ⟨-, hTcard⟩
    refine ⟨T.image σ.symm, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
    · rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ σ.symm.injective, hTcard]
    · rw [Finset.image_image]
      simp

theorem vertexTransitive_skeletonCorpus (d : ℕ) :
    VertexTransitive (skeletonCorpus V d) := fun x y =>
  ⟨Equiv.swap x y, relabel_skeletonCorpus _ d, Equiv.swap_apply_left x y⟩

/-- **Labels are invisible on the extremal corpora.**  For every document size `d`, no
uniform rule recovers any labelling of the theorems that distinguishes two of them from the
complete `d`-uniform design. -/
theorem no_uniform_recovery_design {L : Type*} (R : Corpus V → V → L) (hR : Uniform R)
    (d : ℕ) (lab : V → L) {x y : V} (hxy : lab x ≠ lab y) :
    R (skeletonCorpus V d) ≠ lab :=
  no_uniform_recovery R hR (vertexTransitive_skeletonCorpus d) lab hxy

/-- The witness is homologically rich: the realised profile of the `2`-uniform design on
`n = m + 1` theorems has first Betti number `C(m, 2)`. -/
theorem design_betti_one {m : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card V = m + 1) (hdn : 2 ≤ m + 1) :
    (skeletonHomologyProfile hcard (by norm_num) hdn).beta 1 = m.choose 2 := by
  simp [skeletonHomologyProfile, skeletonBetti]

/-- ... and that first Betti number is positive as soon as there are at least three
theorems, so the non-identifiability above is not an artefact of a topologically trivial
example. -/
theorem design_betti_one_pos {m : ℕ} (hcard : Fintype.card V = m + 1) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    0 < (skeletonHomologyProfile hcard (by norm_num) (by omega : 2 ≤ m + 1)).beta 1 := by
  rw [design_betti_one hcard (by omega)]
  exact Nat.choose_pos hm

omit [Fintype V] in
/-- **Metadata is genuine extra information.**  A rule that does recover a labelling
distinguishing two theorems on a vertex-transitive corpus — for instance the rule that
simply reads the metadata, `fun _ => lab` — is provably *not* uniform.  So uniformity is
exactly the hypothesis carrying the impossibility, and vertex metadata cannot be a
repackaging of the incidence data. -/
theorem not_uniform_of_recovers {L : Type*} (R : Corpus V → V → L)
    {C : Corpus V} (hC : VertexTransitive C) (lab : V → L) {x y : V}
    (hxy : lab x ≠ lab y) (hrec : R C = lab) : ¬ Uniform R := by
  intro hR
  exact no_uniform_recovery R hR hC lab hxy hrec

Extremal topology of co-citation complexes: numerical demonstrations.

A *corpus* on a finite theorem set V is a family of documents, each document being the
set of theorems it cites.  Its *co-citation complex* is the downward closure of that
family: every subset of a bibliography is a face.

This script verifies, by exact computation on small instances, every quantitative claim
of the accompanying theory:

  2. Sharpness of the extremal face count  max f_q = C(n, q)  for q <= d, attained by
     the complete d-uniform design (all d-subsets are documents).
  3. The closed form  chi = 1 - (-1)^d C(n-1, d)  for the design, and the partial
     alternating binomial identity behind it.
  4. The realised Betti profile of the design: beta_0 = 1, beta_{d-1} = C(n-1, d),
     computed independently by exact mod-2 simplicial homology.
  5. The concentration bound  |chi| <= d * max_{k<d} beta_k  and its localised form
     (n-d)^d <= d! (beta_{d-1} + (d-1) n^{d-1} + 1).
  6. The conformality hierarchy: locally conformal at level m, not at level m+1.
  7. The document budget  f_q <= N C(d, q)  and the sparse separation beta_1 < C(n,2).
  8. Non-identifiability of vertex labels on vertex-transitive corpora.

Self-contained: standard library only.

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations, permutations
from math import comb, factorial
from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Face = FrozenSet[int]
Corpus = List[Face]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Complexes, f-vectors and Euler characteristic
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def co_citation_complex(corpus: Corpus) -> Set[Face]:
    """Downward closure of the corpus: all subsets of documents (empty face excluded)."""
    faces: Set[Face] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        items = sorted(doc)
        for size in range(1, len(items) + 1):
            for sub in combinations(items, size):
                faces.add(frozenset(sub))
    return faces


def f_vector(corpus: Corpus, max_size: int) -> List[int]:
    """f_vector(corpus)[q] = number of faces with exactly q vertices (index from 0)."""
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    counts = [0] * (max_size + 1)
    for face in faces:
        if len(face) <= max_size:
            counts[len(face)] += 1
    return counts


def euler_characteristic(corpus: Corpus, n: int) -> int:
    """chi = f_1 - f_2 + f_3 - ...  (unreduced; the empty face is not counted)."""
    counts = f_vector(corpus, n)
    return sum((-1) ** (q - 1) * counts[q] for q in range(1, n + 1))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Exact simplicial homology over GF(2)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _gf2_rank(rows: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    """Rank over GF(2) of a matrix given as an iterable of bitmask rows."""
    pivots: List[int] = []
    rank = 0
    for row in rows:
        cur = row
        for piv in pivots:
            cur = min(cur, cur ^ piv)
        if cur:
            pivots.append(cur)
            pivots.sort(reverse=True)
            rank += 1
    return rank


def betti_numbers_mod2(corpus: Corpus, max_dim: int) -> List[int]:
    """Betti numbers beta_0 .. beta_{max_dim} of the co-citation complex over GF(2)."""
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    by_size: Dict[int, List[Face]] = {}
    for face in faces:
        by_size.setdefault(len(face), []).append(face)
    for size in by_size:
        by_size[size].sort(key=lambda f: sorted(f))

    index: Dict[int, Dict[Face, int]] = {
        size: {face: i for i, face in enumerate(fs)} for size, fs in by_size.items()
    }

    def boundary_rank(size: int) -> int:
        """Rank of the boundary map from faces of `size` vertices to those of size-1."""
        if size <= 1 or size not in by_size or (size - 1) not in by_size:
            return 0
        rows: List[int] = []
        for face in by_size[size]:
            mask = 0
            for v in face:
                sub = face - {v}
                mask |= 1 << index[size - 1][sub]
            rows.append(mask)
        return _gf2_rank(rows)

    betti: List[int] = []
    for k in range(max_dim + 1):
        chain_dim = len(by_size.get(k + 1, []))
        betti.append(chain_dim - boundary_rank(k + 1) - boundary_rank(k + 2))
    return betti


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Corpora
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def design_corpus(n: int, d: int) -> Corpus:
    """The complete d-uniform design: every d-subset of {0,...,n-1} is a document."""
    return [frozenset(c) for c in combinations(range(n), d)]


def design_euler_closed_form(n: int, d: int) -> int:
    """chi = 1 - (-1)^d C(n-1, d)."""
    return 1 - (-1) ** d * comb(n - 1, d)


def design_betti_profile(n: int, d: int) -> List[int]:
    """Predicted profile: beta_0 = 1, beta_{d-1} = C(n-1, d), everything else 0."""
    profile = [0] * d
    profile[0] += 1
    profile[d - 1] += comb(n - 1, d)
    return profile


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Conformality
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def co_citation_graph(corpus: Corpus, n: int) -> Set[Tuple[int, int]]:
    """Edges {x,y} such that some document contains both."""
    edges: Set[Tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        for x, y in combinations(sorted(doc), 2):
            edges.add((x, y))
    return edges


def is_clique(vertices: Sequence[int], edges: Set[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bool:
    return all((min(x, y), max(x, y)) in edges for x, y in combinations(vertices, 2))


def witness_free_cliques(corpus: Corpus, n: int, size: int) -> List[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """Cliques of the given size with no single document containing them."""
    edges = co_citation_graph(corpus, n)
    bad: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    for cand in combinations(range(n), size):
        if not is_clique(cand, edges):
            continue
        if not any(set(cand) <= set(doc) for doc in corpus):
            bad.append(cand)
    return bad


def local_conformality_level(corpus: Corpus, n: int) -> int:
    """Largest m such that every clique of size <= m has a witnessing document."""
    for size in range(1, n + 1):
        if witness_free_cliques(corpus, n, size):
            return size - 1
    return n


def flag_complex_size(corpus: Corpus, n: int) -> int:
    edges = co_citation_graph(corpus, n)
    total = 0
    for size in range(1, n + 1):
        for cand in combinations(range(n), size):
            if is_clique(cand, edges):
                total += 1
    return total

        print(f"{m:>3} | {label:<28} | {level:>11} | {bad}")
    print("  m = 2 is the classical hollow triangle {{0,1},{0,2},{1,2}}:")
    print("   ", sorted(tuple(sorted(w)) for w in design_corpus(3, 2)))
    print()
    print("  pairwise projection invents faces:")
    print(f"  {'n':>3} {'d':>3} | {'true faces':>11} {'flag faces':>11} {'invented':>9}")
    for n, d in [(4, 2), (5, 2), (5, 3), (6, 3)]:
        corpus = design_corpus(n, d)
        true_faces = sum(comb(n, q) for q in range(1, d + 1))
        flag = flag_complex_size(corpus, n)
        assert flag == 2 ** n - 1, "two-section of a design is complete"
        assert len(co_citation_complex(corpus)) == true_faces
        print(f"  {n:>3} {d:>3} | {true_faces:>11} {flag:>11} {flag - true_faces:>9}")
    print("  (counts exclude the empty face; the flag complex has all 2^n subsets.)\n")

    for n, d, N, q in [(50, 3, 40, 2), (50, 3, 40, 3), (200, 4, 500, 3),
                       (1000, 5, 5000, 4)]:
        budget = N * comb(d, q)
        ceiling = comb(n, q)
        assert budget < ceiling, "sparse regime"
        print(f"{n:>4} {d:>3} {N:>6} | {budget:>16} {ceiling:>15} | {q}")
    print()
    print("  explicit pairwise instance: 2-bounded corpus, N <= n documents, n >= 4")
    print(f"  {'n':>4} | {'beta_1 (computed)':>18} {'budget N':>10} {'ceiling C(n,2)':>15}")
    for n in [4, 5, 6, 7]:

        corpus = [frozenset({i, (i + 1) % n}) for i in range(n)]
        betti = betti_numbers_mod2(corpus, 1)

        assert betti[1] < comb(n, 2), "strict sparse separation"

    invariant_under_all = True
    for perm in permutations(range(n)):

        if relabelled != corpus:

corpus whose documents cite at most d theorems: with N documents,

        f_q <= N * C(d, q)        and hence      beta_{q-1} <= N * C(d, q),

corpora, computes their exact modulo-2 Betti numbers, and compares them with
    (a) the realised value,
    (b) the document budget N * C(d, k+1),
    (c) the ambient ceiling C(n, k+1),
showing that the normalised Betti number beta_k / C(n, k+1) collapses towards zero as
soon as the document count grows more slowly than n^{k+1}.

Self-contained: standard library only.  Deterministic (fixed seed).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from itertools import combinations
from math import comb
from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set

Face = FrozenSet[int]


def co_citation_complex(corpus: Sequence[Face]) -> Set[Face]:
    faces: Set[Face] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        items = sorted(doc)
        for size in range(1, len(items) + 1):
            for sub in combinations(items, size):
                faces.add(frozenset(sub))
    return faces


def gf2_rank(rows: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    pivots: List[int] = []
    rank = 0
    for row in rows:
        cur = row
        for piv in pivots:
            cur = min(cur, cur ^ piv)
        if cur:
            pivots.append(cur)
            pivots.sort(reverse=True)
            rank += 1
    return rank


def betti_numbers_mod2(corpus: Sequence[Face], max_dim: int) -> List[int]:
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    by_size: Dict[int, List[Face]] = {}
    for face in faces:
        by_size.setdefault(len(face), []).append(face)
    for size in by_size:
        by_size[size].sort(key=lambda f: sorted(f))
    index = {s: {f: i for i, f in enumerate(fs)} for s, fs in by_size.items()}

    def boundary_rank(size: int) -> int:
        if size <= 1 or size not in by_size or (size - 1) not in by_size:
            return 0
        rows = []
        for face in by_size[size]:
            mask = 0
            for v in face:
                mask |= 1 << index[size - 1][face - {v}]
            rows.append(mask)
        return gf2_rank(rows)

    return [
        len(by_size.get(k + 1, [])) - boundary_rank(k + 1) - boundary_rank(k + 2)
        for k in range(max_dim + 1)
    ]


def random_bounded_corpus(n: int, d: int, N: int, rng: random.Random) -> List[Face]:
    """N documents, each a uniformly random subset of size between 2 and d."""
    corpus: List[Face] = []
    for _ in range(N):
        size = rng.randint(2, d)
        corpus.append(frozenset(rng.sample(range(n), size)))
    return corpus

",
    "design_profile": """"Algorithm A --- Extremal profile evaluation for the complete d-uniform design.

Given a theorem count n and a document-size bound d, this routine returns the complete
extremal data of the maximally symmetric d-bounded corpus (every d-subset of theorems is
a document):

  * the f-vector  f_q = C(n, q)  for 1 <= q <= d, and f_q = 0 for q > d;
  * the Euler characteristic in closed form,  chi = 1 - (-1)^d C(n-1, d),
    obtained from the partial alternating binomial identity
        sum_{j=0}^{d} (-1)^j C(m+1, j) = (-1)^d C(m, d),
    which collapses a length-d alternating sum to a single binomial coefficient;
  * the realised Betti profile  beta_0 = 1,  beta_{d-1} = C(n-1, d),  else 0;
  * the certified concentration bounds
        |chi| <= d * max_{k<d} beta_k                          (pigeonhole form)
        (n-d)^d <= d! (beta_{d-1} + (d-1) n^(d-1) + 1)         (localised form).

Complexity: O(d) big-integer operations (each binomial coefficient is obtained by an
incremental multiply-divide), against O(n d) for a naive alternating summation over the
whole f-vector.  Memory O(d).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from math import comb, factorial
from typing import List


@dataclass
class DesignProfile:
    n: int
    d: int
    f_vector: List[int]          # f_1, ..., f_d
    euler_characteristic: int
    betti: List[int]             # beta_0, ..., beta_{d-1}
    concentration_lhs: int       # |chi|
    concentration_rhs: int       # d * max beta_k
    localised_lhs: int           # (n-d)^d
    localised_rhs: int           # d! (beta_{d-1} + (d-1) n^{d-1} + 1)


def design_profile(n: int, d: int) -> DesignProfile:
    """Extremal profile of the complete d-uniform design on n theorems (1 <= d <= n)."""
    if not (1 <= d <= n):
        raise ValueError("require 1 <= d <= n")

    # f-vector by incremental binomials: C(n, q) = C(n, q-1) * (n-q+1) / q
    f: List[int] = []
    cur = 1
    for q in range(1, d + 1):
        cur = cur * (n - q + 1) // q
        f.append(cur)

    chi = 1 - (-1) ** d * comb(n - 1, d)

    betti = [0] * d
    betti[0] += 1
    betti[d - 1] += comb(n - 1, d)

    return DesignProfile(
        n=n,
        d=d,
        f_vector=f,
        euler_characteristic=chi,
        betti=betti,
        concentration_lhs=abs(chi),
        concentration_rhs=d * max(betti),
        localised_lhs=(n - d) ** d,
        localised_rhs=factorial(d) * (betti[d - 1] + (d - 1) * n ** (d - 1) + 1),
    )


def verify(profile: DesignProfile) -> bool:
    """Check the closed forms against direct summation and the certified inequalities."""
    n, d = profile.n, profile.d
    chi_direct = sum((-1) ** (q - 1) * comb(n, q) for q in range(1, d + 1))
    euler_poincare = sum((-1) ** k * profile.betti[k] for k in range(d))
    return (
        profile.f_vector == [comb(n, q) for q in range(1, d + 1)]
        and chi_direct == profile.euler_characteristic == euler_poincare
        and profile.concentration_lhs <= profile.concentration_rhs
        and profile.localised_lhs <= profile.localised_rhs
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for n, d in [(3, 2), (5, 3), (10, 3), (20, 4), (60, 5)]:
        p = design_profile(n, d)
        assert verify(p)
        print(f"n={p.n:>3} d={p.d}  f={p.f_vector}  chi={p.euler_characteristic}  "
              f"beta={p.betti}")
        print(f"        |chi|={p.concentration_lhs} <= d*max beta="
              f"{p.concentration_rhs};  (n-d)^d={p.localised_lhs} <= "
              f"{p.localised_rhs}")

    "conformality_audit": """"Algorithm B --- Conformality audit of a corpus.

A corpus is *conformal* when its co-citation complex (all subsets of bibliographies)
coincides with the flag complex of its pairwise co-citation graph, i.e. when every clique
of the graph is contained in a single document.  For a d-bounded corpus conformality
splits exactly into

    (i)  a clique-number condition: every clique has at most d vertices;
    (ii) local conformality at level d: every clique of size <= d has a witnessing
         document.

Condition (ii) is verifiable by bounded local search; condition (i) is global, and the
hierarchy theorem shows that for every level m there is a corpus passing all checks up to
size m and failing at size m+1 --- so no bounded local search can ever imply (i).

This audit reports:
    * the largest level m at which the corpus is locally conformal;
    * the minimal witness-free cliques (the certificates of failure);
    * the number of faces invented by the pairwise projection.

Complexity: clique enumeration dominates.  A level-m audit inspects O(n^m) candidate
vertex sets and tests each against the document list, giving O(n^m * (m^2 + N m)) time
with N documents; for the definitive audit m runs up to the clique number, worst case
O(3^{n/3}) maximal cliques.  Space O(n^2 + total face count).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from itertools import combinations
from typing import FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Set, Tuple

Document = FrozenSet[int]


@dataclass
class ConformalityReport:
    n: int
    d: int                                    # max document size
    local_level: int                          # largest m with all cliques <= m witnessed
    clique_number: int
    conformal: bool
    minimal_obstructions: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = field(default_factory=list)
    true_faces: int = 0
    flag_faces: int = 0

    @property
    def invented_faces(self) -> int:
        return self.flag_faces - self.true_faces


def _edges(corpus: Sequence[Document]) -> Set[Tuple[int, int]]:
    e: Set[Tuple[int, int]] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        for x, y in combinations(sorted(doc), 2):
            e.add((x, y))
    return e


def _is_clique(vs: Sequence[int], edges: Set[Tuple[int, int]]) -> bool:
    return all((min(a, b), max(a, b)) in edges for a, b in combinations(vs, 2))


def audit_conformality(corpus: Sequence[Document], n: int) -> ConformalityReport:
    """Full conformality audit of a corpus on the theorem set {0, ..., n-1}."""
    edges = _edges(corpus)
    d = max((len(doc) for doc in corpus), default=0)

    local_level = n
    obstructions: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
    clique_number = 0
    true_faces = 0
    flag_faces = 0

    for size in range(1, n + 1):
        witnessed_all = True
        size_obstructions: List[Tuple[int, ...]] = []
        for cand in combinations(range(n), size):
            if not _is_clique(cand, edges):
                continue
            clique_number = max(clique_number, size)
            flag_faces += 1
            witnessed = any(set(cand) <= set(doc) for doc in corpus)
            if witnessed:
                true_faces += 1
            else:
                witnessed_all = False
                size_obstructions.append(cand)
        if not witnessed_all and local_level == n:
            local_level = size - 1
            obstructions = size_obstructions

    return ConformalityReport(
        n=n,
        d=d,
        local_level=local_level,
        clique_number=clique_number,
        conformal=(local_level == n),
        minimal_obstructions=obstructions,
        true_faces=true_faces,
        flag_faces=flag_faces,
    )


def design(n: int, d: int) -> List[Document]:
    """The complete d-uniform design on n theorems."""
    return [frozenset(c) for c in combinations(range(n), d)]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("hierarchy of obstructions (design corpora D_{m+1,m}):")
    for m in (2, 3, 4):
        rep = audit_conformality(design(m + 1, m), m + 1)
        print(f"  m={m}: local level {rep.local_level}, clique number "
              f"{rep.clique_number}, conformal={rep.conformal}, "
              f"minimal obstructions {rep.minimal_obstructions}")

    print("\nfaces invented by the pairwise projection:")
    for n, d in [(4, 2), (5, 3), (6, 3)]:
        rep = audit_conformality(design(n, d), n)
        print(f"  D_{{{n},{d}}}: true {rep.true_faces}, flag {rep.flag_faces}, "
              f"invented {rep.invented_faces}")

    print("\na conformal corpus (one all-encompassing document):")
    rep = audit_conformality([frozenset(range(5))], 5)
    print(f"  local level {rep.local_level}, conformal={rep.conformal}, "
          f"invented {rep.invented_faces}")

    "mod2_homology": """"Algorithm C --- Exact modulo-2 homology of a co-citation complex.

The co-citation complex of a corpus is the downward closure of its documents.  Its Betti
numbers over the two-element field are

    beta_k = f_{k+1} - rank(d_k) - rank(d_{k+1}),

where f_{k+1} is the number of faces with k+1 vertices and d_k is the boundary map from
faces with k+1 vertices to faces with k vertices (over GF(2) all signs are 1, so the
boundary of a face is the sum of its facets).

Because a d-bounded corpus has no face with more than d vertices, only the dimensions
0, ..., d-1 need be processed: the loop is governed by document size, not by the number
of theorems.

Ranks are computed by Gaussian elimination over GF(2) with each matrix row stored as a
single Python integer used as a bitmask, so a row operation is one XOR.  With f_k faces
in dimension k-1 and f_{k+1} in dimension k the elimination costs
O(f_{k+1} * f_k * min(f_k, f_{k+1}) / w) bit operations for machine word size w.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import combinations
from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Set

Face = FrozenSet[int]


def co_citation_complex(corpus: Sequence[Face]) -> Set[Face]:
    """All nonempty subsets of documents."""
    faces: Set[Face] = set()
    for doc in corpus:
        items = sorted(doc)
        for size in range(1, len(items) + 1):
            for sub in combinations(items, size):
                faces.add(frozenset(sub))
    return faces


def gf2_rank(rows: Iterable[int]) -> int:
    """Rank over GF(2) of a bitmask-row matrix, by elimination on leading bits."""
    pivots: List[int] = []
    rank = 0
    for row in rows:
        cur = row
        for piv in pivots:
            cur = min(cur, cur ^ piv)
        if cur:
            pivots.append(cur)
            pivots.sort(reverse=True)
            rank += 1
    return rank


def betti_numbers_mod2(corpus: Sequence[Face], max_dim: int) -> List[int]:
    """Betti numbers beta_0, ..., beta_{max_dim} of the co-citation complex over GF(2)."""
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    by_size: Dict[int, List[Face]] = {}
    for face in faces:
        by_size.setdefault(len(face), []).append(face)
    for size in by_size:
        by_size[size].sort(key=lambda f: sorted(f))
    index: Dict[int, Dict[Face, int]] = {
        size: {face: i for i, face in enumerate(fs)} for size, fs in by_size.items()
    }

    def boundary_rank(size: int) -> int:
        if size <= 1 or size not in by_size or (size - 1) not in by_size:
            return 0
        rows: List[int] = []
        for face in by_size[size]:
            mask = 0
            for v in face:
                mask |= 1 << index[size - 1][face - {v}]
            rows.append(mask)
        return gf2_rank(rows)

    return [
        len(by_size.get(k + 1, [])) - boundary_rank(k + 1) - boundary_rank(k + 2)
        for k in range(max_dim + 1)
    ]


def euler_characteristic(corpus: Sequence[Face]) -> int:
    faces = co_citation_complex(corpus)
    return sum((-1) ** (len(f) - 1) for f in faces)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    hollow_triangle = [frozenset({0, 1}), frozenset({0, 2}), frozenset({1, 2})]
    filled_triangle = [frozenset({0, 1, 2})]
    octahedron_pairs = [frozenset(c) for c in combinations(range(5), 2)]
    hollow_tetra = [frozenset(c) for c in combinations(range(4), 3)]

    for name, corpus, dim in [
        ("hollow triangle (3 pairwise documents)", hollow_triangle, 1),
        ("one triple document", filled_triangle, 1),
        ("complete pairwise design on 5 theorems", octahedron_pairs, 1),
        ("all triples on 4 theorems", hollow_tetra, 2),

        chi = euler_characteristic(corpus)
        assert sum((-1) ** k * b for k, b in enumerate(beta)) == chi
        print(f"{name:<42} beta={beta}  chi={chi}")
